title: Minimax Transported ATE Estimation with Sparse Cells and Separate Target Covariate Samples
banked_reason: The proposed matched all-regime logarithmic frontier and sharp phase boundaries have been replaced by an explicitly unmatched d/n^2-to-d^2/n^2 bracket.
gap_reasons: The note proves only the bracket with dimension terms d/n^2 below and d^2/n^2 above, so it does not deliver the advertised sharp annotation frontier, matched minimax rate, or sharp growing-alphabet phase boundaries.

The unresolved polynomial envelopes and paired-prior assembly are the substantive contribution originally promised, and without them the paper remains a narrow bracket with conservative planning implications and insufficient novelty and practical evidence for a leading econometrics journal.

The proposed matched all-regime logarithmic frontier and sharp phase boundaries have been replaced by an explicitly unmatched d/n^2-to-d^2/n^2 bracket; retitle and position this weaker delivered theorem as such, or resolve the two open handles before retaining the promised frontier framing.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery pursued a matched logarithmic minimax rate for a transported observational ATE with unknown source propensity and target masses. It proved a sound all-regime bracket, a total observable estimator, occupied-target-support adaptation, and lower-bound transfers, but did not prove the hybrid polynomial estimator envelopes or the paired-prior converse needed to close the dimension gap. The D0.5 math referee passed the delivered claims; the novelty review rated the package incremental, below the field floor.
tldr: The target ATE is identified by averaging transported source conditional effects over an independently sampled target covariate law, but sparse cells make the source and target samples complementary rather than poolable. The proved all-regime result is the honest bracket \(c_{\epsilon}\min\{1,n^{-1}+m^{-1}+d/n^2\}\leq R_{\epsilon}(n,m,d)\leq C_{\epsilon}\min\{1,n^{-1}+m^{-1}+d^2/n^2\}\). The upper witness is the total observable cell-mean estimator; the displayed legal source-only and target-only two-point submodels prove the two parametric floors for every randomized procedure. A uniform homogeneous-effect anchor supplies the inherited \(d/n^2\) collision floor, while a second uniform-covariate anchor gives a constant-risk obstruction under explicitly fixed severe-sparsity constants. The baseline adapts pointwise to occupied target support and, because \(q_x\leq2p_x\), immediately implies the occupied-source-support version. The sharper candidate with dimension term \(d^2/[n^2\log^2(e\min\{n,m\})]\) remains a conjecture until the hybrid envelopes and paired-prior assembly are proved.
gap: Published transport theory supplies identification, regular efficiency, smooth-class minimax results, and applied workflows, while the discrete-ATE literature supplies a supervised logarithmic lower bound and homogeneous endpoints. It does not determine the unknown-law two-sample risk when target observations contain only covariates and arbitrary occupied-cell effects must be averaged under a shifted target mass.
fill: The project seeks one matched theorem over the published transport identification model specialized to an unrestricted finite alphabet: a total observable hybrid estimator, an all-procedure paired-prior converse, and necessary-and-sufficient consistency and parametric-risk phase boundaries.
